question: A building contractor employs 25 male and 15 female workers. To a male worker he pays ₹20 per hour and to a female worker ₹20 per hour. The average wage per hour paid by the contractor is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the **wage per hour** for both **male workers** and **female workers** is the same (₹20), the **average wage** must also be ₹20.

Equal rates for all groups → Average = Rate.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of **male workers** = 25

Wage of **male worker** = ₹20 per hour

Number of **female workers** = 15

Wage of **female worker** = ₹20 per hour

**Formula Used:**

Average Wage = (Total Wages) ÷ (Total Number of Workers)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f11532251b426b280655c9b49ffdda1b2c42aedfed3ba93f13e55745fa6d2a7f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total wage of males = 25 × 20 = ₹500

⇒ Total wage of females = 15 × 20 = ₹300

⇒ Total number of workers = 25 + 15 = 40

⇒ Total wages paid = 500 + 300 = ₹800

⇒ Average wage = 800 ÷ 40

⇒ Average wage = ₹20

**∴ The correct answer is ₹20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When groups have different sizes (n₁, n₂) and different values (x₁, x₂), the average is (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Constant Value Rule

If every observation in a data set is a constant **k**, then the **arithmetic mean** of the data set is also **k**.
